summary: Iteration 112 — Validated the async refactor of POST /api/agent/courses/{project_id}/apply-improvements + new GET /apply-status/{job_id}. Backend: 13/13 tests pass (5 pre-existing apply_improvements_retry + 8 new apply_improvements_async_flow). Confirmed: endpoint returns in <2s with {status:'processing', applyJobId, startedAt}, idempotency reuses an in-flight processing job's id, anonymous→401, cross-company→404, bogus previewId→400, missing previewId→fresh path, background worker reaches status='done' with progress/message and the cached preview is deleted after success, apply-status enforces auth + RBAC + 404 on bogus job. Frontend: Agent page loads cleanly via REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL with no console errors; polling loop in handleConfirmImprovements (Agent.jsx:923-1000) and the data-testid='apply-progress-panel' in CoursePanels.jsx:1271 are correctly wired (gated on applyProgress state).
critical_code_review_comments: agent.py is 3982 lines — keep splitting (the apply_improvements + _run_apply_improvements_bg + _process_* helpers ~540 lines is a clean extract candidate to routes/agent_apply.py).

The background worker creates a NEW AsyncIOMotorClient per job (routes/agent.py:2858-2860). For high-frequency apply requests this leaks connection pools — consider a module-level lazy client keyed by event loop, or close the client in the finally branch of _run_apply_improvements_bg.
apply_jobs collection has no TTL index; old 'done' / 'error' jobs accumulate. Suggest a TTL index on startedAt or a startup cleanup of jobs older than 24h.

Idempotency check (line 2772) is read-then-write without a unique index; a true race between two simultaneous POSTs could insert two processing rows. Mitigation: add a partial unique index on apply_jobs (projectId, status='processing') or wrap insert in a try/except DuplicateKey.

Frontend polling in handleConfirmImprovements (Agent.jsx:962-966) silently ignores statusRes.ok=false during transient errors — good resilience — but a 401 from token expiry will loop forever until MAX_WAIT_MS. Consider treating 401/403 as terminal.

success_rate.frontend: smoke OK (Agent page loads, no console errors); deep apply-flow not driven E2E (requires real LLM preview)

seed_data_creation: Tests insert temporary improvement_previews + one fake apply_jobs row, all cleaned up in finally blocks (no production data mutated).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Async apply-improvements flow is fully covered by /app/backend/tests/test_apply_improvements_async_flow.py (8 tests) + test_apply_improvements_retry.py (5 tests). Both files are independent and can be run with `BASE_URL=$REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL pytest backend/tests/test_apply_improvements_*.py`. Frontend visual progress bar (data-testid='apply-progress-panel') was not driven through a real apply because that requires a real preview-improvements run (slow/LLM dependent). The polling code (Agent.jsx:923-1000) was code-reviewed and is correct. Pre-existing failing tests (test_apply_improvements_fix.py::test_08 brittle assertion, test_preview_undo_improvements.py::MissingSchema) are unchanged and unrelated to this refactor — DO NOT report them as regressions.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. The async refactor is correctly implemented: endpoint returns in <2s with applyJobId, daemon thread + new event loop + dedicated AsyncIOMotorClient runs the BG work, idempotency reuses in-flight jobs, RBAC enforced via load_authorized_project, preview persistence preserved on failure (only deleted on success), apply-status returns proper 401/404. One race-condition mitigation suggested (DuplicateKey on apply_jobs) but not exploitable in practice.
